newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Nickles - resolve economic assumption gap.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Nickles - resolve economic assumption gap.

text.p: Assistant Senate Majority Leader Don Nickles on Wednesday said the White House and Congress must resolve their differences in economic assumptions used for crafting the budget.
"There's not a great deal of difference" between the two economic assumptions, Nickles said, adding that the gap was about $190 billion over five years.

"I think very soon ... if the administration's going to play with us and we're going to work, we have to be working off the same data sheet," Nickles said. "It's very hard to negotiate budgets and compromises if one side assumes a much rosier scenario than the other," he added.
Nickles said he hoped a budget package would be put together by June, followed by the appropriations process in September.
There will also be a tax cut package this year, he told reporters.

"I want tax cuts ... we're not walking away from tax cuts in any way, shape or form," Nickles said. "There is a legitimate strategy -- do you want to put everything in one great big bill? -- and I'm not sure that's always the wisest," he said, noting that the welfare bill passed separately last year.
"We're going to get a tax package this year," the Oklahoma Republican said. There is bipartisan support for estate, capital gains and child tax relief, he said.
